items.t: High-pressure fuel pump failure
items.job: Replace high-pressure pump, injectors and fuel lines; clean the tank
items.note: One F-450 owner reported about $11,700 for this repair. A pump-only repair caught before debris spreads costs much less.

items.t: Oil cooler and EGR cooler failure leading to head gasket trouble
items.job: Replace engine oil cooler and EGR cooler
items.note: F-550 owners report about $2,800 on average for EGR repairs. If head gaskets have failed, head studs and gaskets add a lot more.

items.t: EGR cooler failure and coolant blowing out of the reservoir
items.job: Replace head gaskets with head studs and EGR cooler (cab off)
items.note: One F-450 owner paid about $6,000. An EGR cooler alone costs less, but lifting the cab adds 4 to 8 hours.

items.t: Radiator leaks at the plastic tank seam
items.job: Replace radiator
items.note: F-450 owners report about $800 with some doing their own labor; shop prices for a Super Duty radiator can run near $2,700 or more.

items.t: Fuel tank lining flakes and clogs the fuel system
items.job: Replace fuel tank and filters, flush fuel lines
items.note: F-550 owners report about $2,200 to $3,500. Damaged injectors or a fuel pump add a lot more.

items.t: Camshaft position sensor can fail and stall the engine (recall)
items.job: Replace camshaft position sensor
items.note: Covered by a Ford recall. If done outside the recall, ask the shop for a written quote.

items.t: Spark plugs seize and break during removal
items.job: Replace spark plugs, extracting any that break
items.note: Ford pays labor at actual time for this job because broken plugs take extra work to extract.

items.t: Exhaust manifold studs break, causing a ticking exhaust leak
items.job: Extract broken exhaust manifold studs, install new studs and gasket
items.note: Broken studs take extra time to remove, which can raise the labor a lot.

items.t: Exhaust temperature sensor fault can shut the engine off (recall)
items.job: Replace exhaust temperature sensor(s) and update software
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Fuel line connector can separate and leak fuel (recall)
items.job: Replace fuel jumper line
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Low-pressure fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
items.job: Replace low-pressure fuel pump
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Fuel pump deposits can cause stalling (recall)
items.job: Update engine software and inspect the fuel system
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Steering wheel shake after bumps (steering damper program)
items.job: Replace steering linkage damper
items.note: Free under Ford program 20N04 for 7 years or 100,000 miles from the truck's warranty start date, so many trucks are now past it. Ford lists 0.4 hour to replace the damper (part KC3Z-3E651-B); we could not find a current part price. Check with a Ford dealer.

items.t: Steering gear can bind or lose steering (recall)
items.job: Inspect and replace steering gear
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Steering column shaft bolts may be loose or missing (recall)
items.job: Inspect and install or tighten steering shaft bolts
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Front wheel hub extenders may be loose and a wheel can come off (recall)
items.job: Inspect and torque front hub extender fasteners
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Driveline vibration can break the driveline or transmission (recall)
items.job: Inspect and repair driveline per recall
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Brake pedal pushrod can disconnect (recall)
items.job: Inspect and install brake pushrod retaining spring
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Cruise control deactivation switch can overheat and catch fire (recall)
items.job: Install fused wiring or replace the deactivation switch
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Turn signals and brake lights may stop working (recall)
items.job: Replace multi-function switch
items.note: Covered by a Ford recall. Outside the recall, ask the shop for a written quote.

items.t: PTO pressure switch can leak oil onto the exhaust (recall)
items.job: Inspect PTO pressure switch; replace or plug the port
items.note: Free under the upfitter's recall. Check with the body builder or dealer.

items.t: Engine block heater cord can overheat (recall)
items.job: Replace block heater cord
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Seat belt pretensioner sparks can start a fire (recall)
items.job: Add heat shield and modify pillar trim
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Backup camera image may be blank, distorted or upside down (recall)
items.job: Replace rear camera
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Backup camera may freeze, lag or go blank (recall)
items.job: Update camera software or replace camera
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Windshield wiper arms may break (recall)
items.job: Replace windshield wiper arms
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Trailer brake module can lose connection while towing (recall)
items.job: Update trailer module software
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Driver airbag may not deploy due to clock spring fault (recall)
items.job: Replace steering wheel clock spring
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Instrument cluster may fail or gauges read wrong (recall)
items.job: Update or replace instrument cluster
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: LED headlights may fail (recall)
items.job: Replace LED headlamp assembly
items.note: Covered by a Ford safety recall at no cost. Check your VIN or ask a Ford dealer.

items.t: Injector control module (FICM) failure
items.job: Reprogram and replace the fuel injection control module (FICM) or its power-supply half
items.note: Ford TSB 10-12-6 lists 0.5 hour to reprogram and 1.7 hours to reprogram and replace the module or its half shell. Rebuilt modules sell for about $300; an upgraded new module is about $1,250, and an owner was quoted about $1,000 at a dealer. Test and replace weak batteries first.

items.t: Spark plug blown out of the cylinder head
items.job: Install a thread insert in the cylinder head and a new spark plug
items.note: The kit maker says the insert can go in, with the head on the engine, in as little as 25 minutes; reaching the plug and coil adds time. A single insert is about $20 and a full kit about $300–$385. If the threads can't take an insert, the head has to come off, which costs much more.

items.t: Fuel in the oil from soot filter cleaning cycles
items.job: Oil and filter change (at shorter intervals)
items.note: There is no single part that cures this; the usual fix is changing the oil more often and avoiding lots of short trips. The 6.4L takes about 15 quarts of diesel-rated oil.

items.t: Turbocharger failure on early 6.7L diesels
items.job: Replace turbocharger with a remanufactured or updated steel-bearing unit
items.note: A remanufactured pickup turbo is about $1,454 plus a core deposit; OEM turbos run about $1,800–$2,500. Hours are worked out from Bostech's shop labor figure of $800–$1,500. 2012 F-250 owners report $3,920–$4,493 total. Cab-and-chassis trucks use a different turbo, so parts prices vary.
